title: Multithreading & Stakeholder Mapping
headline: Map the people behind the decision.
eyebrow: Field practice · Illustrative model · Short read
standfirst: Use the same fictional software-company security evaluation as the enterprise deal walkthrough. Map decision roles, separate access from influence, and identify which conversations need validation.
metaDescription: How I think about complex buying groups: a short field note, an interactive stakeholder example, and a deeper walkthrough by request.
limitations: Stakeholders, relationships and access states are fictional. This preview does not read private account systems. Coverage does not prove influence, budget approval or purchase intent.

sections.body: For the seller, the map suggests a next conversation. For the sales leader, it makes access gaps and untested assumptions easier to coach. Every stakeholder and relationship in the example is fictional.
the opportunity relies on one contact or the decision roles are unclear. Try one gap in the synthetic map, then decide which conversation would test it.

sections.heading: Who matters?
sections.body: Map decision roles and affected teams, beyond the people already in the meeting.

sections.heading: What is validated?
sections.body: Separate access from influence. A responsive contact is not automatically a champion or budget owner.

sections.heading: Why another conversation?
sections.body: Connect each introduction to a stakeholder’s priorities and the decision the group needs to make.

sections.heading: What the example reveals
sections.body: The security champion and technical evaluator are engaged, but budget authority is still unvalidated. I would use the next conversation to understand the approval path and earn a business-outcome discussion. As a coach, I would ask what evidence supports that introduction and who owns the next action.

sections.heading: Go deeper into the approach.
sections.body: Request a conversation about stakeholder planning, champion validation, and how I would coach the next move. I’ll review the request and confirm which walkthrough or sanitized materials I can share.
sections.note: Requests do not automatically unlock files. Detailed materials are shared separately after review, where available.

sections.body: Account research can suggest who to involve; customer conversations validate their priorities and influence.
